classification.theory_summary: Proposes that large public labyrinth-like interiors (malls, schools) are used in dreams because early childhood experiences of vast overstimulating spaces leave lasting unconscious resonance; dreams convert abstract thoughts/emotions into visual/spatial/tactile forms using memory.
classification.skip_reason: No specific dream episode described; post is a general theory about why malls/schools appear in dreams.

meta.author_theory: Large, vast, public, labyrinth-like interiors (malls, schools) resonate unconsciously due to impactful first childhood exposures; dreams render abstract thoughts/emotions into visual/spatial/tactile forms using stored memories; these spaces convey anxiety or wonder in adulthood.

extraction.extraction_notes: Post contains only generalized setting descriptors (e.g., 'vast, public structure of a mall', 'large labyrinth-type interiors') without a concrete dream narrative, specific locations, movements, entities, or events to extract.
